newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-HENDRY IN SIGHT OF ANOTHER WORLD FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-HENDRY IN SIGHT OF ANOTHER WORLD FINAL.

text.p: Titleholder Stephen Hendry looked set on Saturday to take his place in the final of the world snooker championship as he powered to a 14-10 lead over Thailand's James Wattana.
The pair had resumed their semifinal at 8-8 and the Scot took the next four frames even though his opponent had several chances to take control of each of the frames.
Wattana did manage to claw a frame back with a break of 77 and then a break of 75 left him just two frames down.
But it was only a brief respite as Hendry kept his cool and Wattana again failed to take his chances.
Hendry moved to 13-10 despite leaving two reds on the table after a break of 55.

Wattana could not pot them and the Scot returned to clear up. He then edged the next frame to go into Saturday night's session needing just three more frames for the right to meet Ireland's Ken Doherty in the final.
Doherty beat Canada's Alain Robidoux 17-7 in the other semifinal.
